target.paraphrase: Released case-specific questions directly check support, flow direction, contact-mediated propagation, solid non-penetration and teleportation. For example: unsupported floating blocks (case_001), upward water flow (006), cup interpenetration (008), soup through a solid pot side (013), dominoes falling without neighbor contact (014), item through solid box wall (033), marbles through glass walls (045), block teleportation (046), blocks through solid tray walls (047). All named violation questions have expected_answer=no. These are physical transition constraints beyond final-state or persistence questions.

The parser requires four categories with two questions each; causal_physics occupies the last two positions. Actual question text and expected answers come from the frozen per-case annotations. The category name is not used as sole evidence for Target P.

protocol.location: vlm.py generate_answers L100-115 and build_prompt L118-186
protocol.paraphrase: The completed generated video is sampled at stride 8 including the first and last frames. The VLM receives ordered images and planned phase ranges; its answers do not change later generation or actions. This supports OL.

metrics.paraphrase: Each yes/no prediction is matched to its frozen expected_answer. If event_started is no, every item is set to zero. causal_physics_score is the mean of the two causal_physics item scores. The per-model benchmark uses the same 60 cases. This is a direct video-output diagnostic (metric class P).
The paper specifies the same 60-case event-start gate and two-question aspect means; the official public manifest and code instantiate this definition.
